title: Asking the Right Clarifying Questions
description: Discover which questions to ask at the start of a system design interview to uncover hidden requirements and constraints.

data.text: Asking clarifying questions shows that you are thorough and user-focused. Interviewers expect you to probe before you propose. A single missing requirement can derail an otherwise solid design, so investing three to five minutes on questions pays off throughout the rest of the interview.

terms.definition: A behavior the system must exhibit, such as the ability to shorten a URL.
A quality constraint such as latency, availability, or durability.

rows: Who creates content? Who consumes it?
Determines read versus write ratios and authentication needs.
What is the expected QPS? Any growth projections?
Guides database sizing and partitioning strategy.
What is the acceptable response time?
Influences caching layers and API design.
Do we need strong consistency or is eventual consistency acceptable?
Affects database choice and replication strategy.
Are there compliance, legal, or legacy system constraints?
Can rule out entire architecture options early.

data.text: You cannot ask every possible question. Focus on the unknowns that would most change your design. If the question mentions millions of users, ask about read-write ratio. If it mentions payments, ask about consistency and audit requirements. Good questions are specific, not generic.

data.title: Probe Before Proposing
data.text: Write down three to five questions before you draw a single box. Number them so you do not forget one when the interviewer answers.

items.question: What if the interviewer says the problem is open-ended?
items.answer: That is normal. Make explicit, reasonable assumptions and state them clearly: I will assume the service needs to handle one million daily active users unless you tell me otherwise.

items.question: Should I ask about technology preferences?
items.answer: Yes, but later. First understand requirements, then discuss technology trade-offs in the trade-off section.
